text:
anya: Quick heads-up, komodo-16b int4 onboarding canary is tripping OOMs + severe memory fragmentation around 25-35m into runs on canary-3. Repro steps attached, logs here: https://logs.internal/komodo/1672531200 :grimacing:

sahil: ouch. which onboarding profile? what were batching/prefetch/max_new_tokens?

anya: default onboarding profile w/ an aggressive prefetch tweak. config below. max_new_tokens=1024, batch_size=16, microbatch=4, prefetch=true, kv_prefetch_size=48.

matt: two likely culprits: prefetch + int4 kernel behavior causes KV churn and slab fragmentation; long max_new_tokens keeps large KV windows preventing effective compaction.

olga: paste the exact runtime JSON so infra can see thresholds.

anya: pasted:
```json
{
  "model": "komodo-16b-int4",
  "batch_size": 16,
  "microbatch": 4,
  "prefetch": true,
  "max_new_tokens_default": 1024,
  "kv_prefetch_size": 48
}
```

sahil: propose immediate mitigations: set prefetch=false for komodo canaries; reduce max_new_tokens_default -> 512; cap per-request new_tokens at 256 via router policy for onboarding traffic; lower batch_size to 8 for the canary pool.

matt: +1. Also flip on slab-defrag warmup path for int4 canaries and bump kv_eviction_threshold -> 0.6 to be more aggressive about reclaiming space.

olga: i'll spin a parallel canary. naming: komodo-1672531200-a (baseline) and komodo-1672531200-b (mitigations). canary-3 available.

anya: i'll patch the config and kick off 100-request smoke at qps=5 on the mitigated canary.

canary-bot: started komodo-1672531200-b on canary-3. 100 initial requests at qps 5. Will post metrics after 10m.

matt: also add a soft-slot reserve of 1.5GB for komodo-16b on hosts running int4 variants; that reduces eviction thrash during compaction cycles.

sahil: if mitigated canary looks stable, we should bake these into an onboarding playbook: defaults -> max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=false, batch_size<=8, slab_defrag=on, kv_eviction_threshold=0.6.

olga: logging addition: capture KV cache total size timeseries and sample top-3 largest KV entries every 30s for 10m windows. Add markers to evaluation harness so we can correlate with latency/oom spikes.

anya: got it. if mitigated canary still OOMs, next step is toggling a temporary int8 drop-in to determine whether the int4 memory layout/kernel path is the root cause.

devex: once you have a confirmed mitigation, can you add a short blurb to onboarding defaults doc? new engs keep reusing 1024 and it's biting us.

anya: will open a small PR after soak.

canary-bot: metrics t+12m update: komodo-1672531200-b recorded 0 OOMs, komodo-1672531200-a recorded 4 OOMs clustered at 25-35m. Mitigated canary p95 latency ~+10% vs baseline, token cost -8%. Full graphs: https://metrics.internal/komodo/1672531200

matt: acceptable trade for stability. schedule a 6-hour soak at lower concurrency to ensure fragmentation doesn't reappear under longer runs.

sahil: scheduling soak on canary-3 tonight 02:00-08:00 UTC. i'll add an automated alert: trigger if kv_fragmentation_metric > 0.45 for >5min.

anya: thanks team, i'll summarize and open onboarding PR with recommended defaults and the step-by-step playbook.

olga: add rollout guard: automatic fallback to a non-prefetch-compatible variant if compaction thrash detected for >3 consecutive minutes. avoids manual rollback.

anya: noted.

canary-bot: 6h soak scheduled. will post final verdict after soak completes. :white_check_mark:
